C-1.why: C-1 dried cranberries from the new supplier Kestrel, an ingredient the November 2025 plan lacks (D-1, D-6); first delivered 12 August 2026 (R-10), so the change is made. Weighted 75 dollars, an hour of a certifier's administrative time

C-2.why: C-2 the second warehouse, Dock B, in use for organic ingredients since 1 July 2026 (D-7); the plan names only Dock A (D-1), so the change is made. Weighted 75 dollars, an hour of a certifier's administrative time

C-3.why: C-3 a second oat roaster, to be installed on 9 March 2027 (D-8); the update also lists the additions planned for the coming year (205.406(a)), so it is reported as planned. Weighted 75 dollars, an hour of a certifier's administrative time

traps.C-4: C-4 the second drying line was reported on 15 April 2026 and accepted on 29 April 2026 (Certifield's accepted changes); it is already in the plan and is not reported again
traps.C-5: C-5 the pouch filler order was cancelled on 12 May 2026 and the machine was never delivered or installed (D-9); nothing changed

S-2.why: S-2 Honeyfield Apiary supplies organic honey; its paper certificate runs to 30 June 2026 (D-3) but the registry shows it suspended on 12 June 2026 (O-2). Weighted 75 dollars, an hour of a certifier's administrative time

S-3.why: S-3 Sunmere Almond Growers supplies organic almonds; the registry shows the certification expired on 31 March 2026 and was not renewed (O-3, D-4). Weighted 75 dollars, an hour of a certifier's administrative time

traps.S-1: S-1 Verdane Oats Cooperative: its paper certificate ran out on 30 April 2025 (D-2) but the registry shows it certified and renewed to 30 April 2027 (O-1); the status is read in the registry, so nothing lapsed
traps.S-4: S-4 Pellwick Pantry Supply has no registry listing because it is exempt under 7 CFR 205.101(e), selling only sealed sacks packed by the certified Ridgeback Seed Co. (D-5, O-10); an exempt supplier is not a lapsed certificate
traps.S-5: S-5 Tamarind Coast Cashews expired on 31 December 2025 (O-4), but its cashews go only into the non-organic Harvest Trail Mix (D-14, D-15), which is outside the plan

R-04.why: R-04 organic coconut oil from the Philippines, 4,200 kg; certificate NOP-IC-26-004172 in the registry covers 4,200 kg (D-10). Weighted 75 dollars, an hour of a certifier's administrative time

R-05.why: R-05 organic cinnamon from Sri Lanka, 600 kg; certificate NOP-IC-26-005031 covers 600 kg (D-11). Weighted 75 dollars, an hour of a certifier's administrative time

R-06.why: R-06 organic cacao nibs from Ecuador, 2,400 kg; certificate NOP-IC-26-006288 covers 2,400 kg (D-12). Weighted 75 dollars, an hour of a certifier's administrative time

traps.R-07: R-07 organic vanilla from Madagascar: the bill of lading and the receipt say 260 kg but certificate NOP-IC-26-007415 covers 200 kg (D-13), so its data do not match the shipment and it is not logged as compliant
traps.R-01: R-01 organic oats from Verdane, bought in the United States: a domestic purchase needs no NOP Import Certificate
traps.R-08: R-08 cashews from Vietnam: an import of a non-organic product for the Harvest Trail Mix (D-14), which needs no NOP Import Certificate
